author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: Slack audit logs come with Enterprise plans and are pull only, through the Audit Logs API, so these parsers read the entries the example bridge in bridges/slack-audit-logs polls and posts to HTTP Ingest, with "slack_record": "audit" first. Give the bridge the user token (xoxp-) of an app with only the auditlogs:read scope that an Org Owner installed on the Enterprise organization. Sign-ins go to Auth: user_login, user_login_failed, cli_login (the Slack CLI) and every user_logout action, a sign-out or one Slack forced, such as user_logout_compromised, with the member's email, the source address, the user agent and the session. Slack's anomaly entries go to Thirdparty, with the first three reason codes (such as ip_address, asn) as the title and the details Slack gives (previous address and user agent, detected client) as additional data; Slack gives anomalies no severity. Every other entry goes to CloudAudit with the action as the event name, the entity type (such as user, channel, file, app or enterprise) as the event type, the actor as the user, a user entity as the target user, the entity and any app as resources, and the previous and new values and scopes in details as request parameters. Downloads, opens, views and exports are read-only, and file, message, canvas, list and huddle actions are data, not management events. Samples follow the entry shape and examples in Slack's Audit Logs API docs and anomalous events reference, with made-up values. Slack publishes no example of user_login_failed, user_logout_compromised, role_change_to_admin, pref.sso_setting_changed, app_scopes_expanded or user_session_reset_by_admin, so those are built from the entry shape, the action list and the details keys in Slack's Python SDK. Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-22 (182 of 182 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and the parent's confirm string picked the same records there. Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (182 of 182 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs). No built-in parser claimed these records.
